items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Rudy Palmer, my lead alto, was very important to me then, teaching the other saxophone players the way to make a tone for section work

ctx.x: But you had the men, too. A lot of men were conscientious. They all were playing saxophone. When we came together they had different makes of instruments. All the brass players went to Bach instruments, Bach flugelhorns and Bach trombones. They did everything to get this ensemble we got. They didn't leave one stone unturned and they were

conscientious about it. Because Rudy Palmer, my lead alto, was very important to me then, teaching the other saxophone players the way to make a tone for section work, (inaudible) because he had studied this with a fine teacher and he got Ben -- they didn't play the same when they took their solos as when they played in the section, to get the blend of the horns. So my band was working on those sort of values. I'm very proud of, and oh, it was really a bitter pill when it had to go. We just couldn't keep our…

Then, too, John Hammond, he didn't believe in it. He could have kept us going but he didn't get behind Willard Alexander, the booking agents, to keep us busy. So they just used us like a football, selling us cheap and telling us they couldn't get no money for us. I couldn't hold the band together, the payrolls, you know. (Inaudible).
